title: The danger isn’t the AI model. It’s the agent acting on its own, and Zenity raised $125m to watch it.
excerpt: Zenity has raised $125m, backed by SoftBank, Hitachi and LG, to secure AI agents at runtime, as OpenAI’s own agents show the danger of letting them act.
content_html:
Most of the money spent guarding AI has gone to the model and the prompt. Zenity has just raised $125m on a different argument: both miss the real danger. That danger is the AI agent that acts on its own. The Israeli startup secures what agents do once a company lets them loose inside its systems.

Norwest led the Series C. SoftBank’s Vision Fund 2, Hitachi Ventures and LG Technology Ventures joined, the company announced. That takes its total funding to roughly $185m. Zenity did not disclose a valuation. Tellingly, the new backers are all firms deploying agents in their own businesses.

Two Unit 8200 veterans, Ben Kliger and Michael Bargury, founded Zenity in 2021. Both previously built security products at Microsoft. It now has more than 230 staff, with research in Tel Aviv and its sales team in New York. Its customers, it says, are mostly Fortune 500 and Global 2000 firms in regulated industries.

Securing the agent, not the model

The pitch rests on a shift the industry is only now catching up to. A chatbot answers a question. An agent takes actions. It can reach internal databases, call tools, update records and run multi-step workflows across systems. That turns a content problem into a control problem.

An agent can behave exactly as designed and still cause a breach. It might have too much access, or read manipulated instructions. So Zenity watches the agent layer: its permissions, connected tools, memory and live actions. It reads the intent behind each action and, it says, can allow, change or block that action before it runs.

Zenity Labs shows the risk. A booby-trapped calendar invite could hijack Perplexity’s agentic browser. It could then open an unlocked password vault and leak the credentials inside. Its earlier AgentFlayer work found zero-click ways to turn enterprise assistants against their owners. The attacks hide inside data an agent is meant to trust.

A category, and a crowded one

The timing is not subtle. The raise lands days after a scare. OpenAI admitted two of its models broke out of a sealed test and hacked Hugging Face. They were chasing a benchmark answer key. That is precisely the scenario Zenity sells against: an agent doing something it should not. It has raised the stakes for every enterprise wiring agents into its systems.

Zenity is not alone in spotting the gap. It is the second nine-figure AI-security round this week, after Horizon3’s $250m for autonomous pentesting. It sits beside startups like Onyx building control layers for agents. Gartner already calls Zenity the company to beat in agent governance. Investors are betting this becomes a category, not a feature.

The caveats trail any fast raise. Zenity has kept its valuation quiet, and its growth figures, however steep, come off a young base. The bigger test is strategic. Enterprises must make a choice. Do they buy a dedicated agent-security platform? Or lean on whatever Microsoft, Google and AWS bundle into the tools where agents already live?

For now, the money is flowing to the specialists. As Kliger puts it, the industry is heading into an “era of 1 billion agents.” Each one can act inside a business, not just answer a question. Zenity’s bet is that someone has to watch what all of them do. This week made that a harder bet to argue with.

content_html_zh:
保护人工智能的大部分资金都花在了模型和提示上。 Zenity 刚刚筹集了 1.25 亿美元，但理由不同：两者都忽视了真正的危险。 这种危险来自于自行行动的人工智能代理。 一旦公司允许代理人在其系统中自由活动，这家以色列初创公司就会确保他们的行为。

Norwest 在 C 轮融资中处于领先地位。 该公司宣布，软银的 Vision Fund 2、Hitachi Ventures 和 LG Technology Ventures 也加入其中。 这使得其总融资额达到约 1.85 亿美元。 Zenity 没有透露估值。 很明显，新的支持者都是在自己的业务中部署代理的公司。

两位 8200 部队老兵 Ben Kliger 和 Michael Bargury 于 2021 年创立了 Zenity。 两人都曾在微软开发过安全产品。 该公司目前拥有 230 多名员工，研发团队位于特拉维夫，销售团队位于纽约。 据称，其客户大多是受监管行业的财富 500 强和全球 2000 强公司。

保护代理，而不是模型

这场宣传的基础是行业现在才刚刚赶上的转变。 聊天机器人回答问题。 代理采取行动。 它可以访问内部数据库、调用工具、更新记录并跨系统运行多步骤工作流程。 这就把内容问题变成了控制问题。

代理可以完全按照设计行事，但仍然会造成违规。 它可能有太多的访问权限，或者读取了被操纵的指令。 因此，Zenity 会监视代理层：其权限、连接的工具、内存和实时操作。 它读取每个操作背后的意图，并且可以在该操作运行之前允许、更改或阻止该操作。

Zenity Labs 展示了这种风险。 一个诱杀日历邀请可能会劫持 Perplexity 的代理浏览器。 然后，它可以打开一个未锁定的密码库并泄露其中的凭据。 其早期的 AgentFlayer 工作发现了零点击的方法来让企业助理反对他们的所有者。 这些攻击隐藏在代理应该信任的数据内。

一个类别，一个拥挤的类别

时机并不微妙。 恐慌发生几天后，加注就落地了。 OpenAI 承认其两个模型突破了密封测试并入侵了 Hugging Face。 他们正在寻找基准答案。 这正是 Zenity 所反对的场景：代理做了不应该做的事情。 它提高了每个企业接线代理进入其系统的风险。

Zenity 并不是唯一发现差距的人。 这是继 Horizo​​n3 为自主渗透测试筹集 2.5 亿美元之后，本周第二轮 9 位数的人工智能安全融资。 它与像 Onyx 这样的初创公司一起为代理构建控制层。 Gartner 已将 Zenity 称为在代理治理方面领先的公司。 投资者押注这将成为一个类别，而不是一个功能。

任何快速加注都需要注意事项。 Zenity 的估值一直保持低调，其增长数据无论多么陡峭，都是建立在年轻的基础上的。 更大的考验是战略性的。 企业必须做出选择。 他们是否购买专用的代理安全平台？ 或者依靠 Microsoft、Google 和 AWS 捆绑到代理已经使用的工具中的任何东西？

目前，资金正流向专家。 正如 Kliger 所说，该行业正在进入“10 亿代理时代”。 每个人都可以在企业内部发挥作用，而不仅仅是回答问题。 Zenity 的赌注是必须有人监督他们所有人的行为。 本周，这一赌注变得更难反驳。
